clue.text: Drink coming from north London district, black stuff!

parts.note: EC is the East Central postal district of London, covering the City
tar is the black sticky stuff used on roads

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys a pint of stout, the black stuff, in a north London district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The black stuff' suggests Guinness, which fits 'Drink', but it is TAR; the drink is that of the gods.
explanation.definitionFit: Nectar is the drink of the gods in Greek myth, and loosely any delicious beverage.

clue.text: Recently made time for dreamy style of music

parts.note: something recently made is new
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A freshly composed piece is timed for a hazy, dreamy genre of music.
explanation.definitionFit: New age is a gentle, atmospheric genre of instrumental music meant for relaxation and meditation.

clue.text: Made plenty of money having removed a peduncle

explanation.surface: Someone made a fortune by snipping off a flower stalk.
explanation.walkthrough: A peduncle is a stalk bearing a flower or fruit; pulling the stalks off fruit is tidying it ready to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a killing financially is slang for a big profit, while tidying fruit by stripping its stalks is literal cleaning.

clue.text: A rigid support so revolutionary incidentally

parts.note: a prop is a rigid support holding something up

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns round, so the word so is read backwards

explanation.surface: A stiff brace that is, by the way, revolutionary in design.
explanation.definitionFit: Apropos, used as an aside, means by the way or in passing, much like the adverb given.

clue.text: Jam on part of the face from the pudding

parts.note: to jam something is to make it stick fast
the jaw is part of the face

explanation.surface: Someone smears jam on their chin while eating dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jam' looks like a noun for the preserve but is the verb, to stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Stickjaw is an old slang name for a stodgy pudding or chewy toffee that glues the teeth together.

clue.text: Consider the matter closed

parts.note: read as an instruction to ponder, it means to reflect on a question; read whimsically, it is to judge an issue finished and done with

explanation.surface: A chairman declares a dispute settled and the subject closed.
explanation.definitionFit: To ponder or reflect carefully before deciding is the idiom's meaning, with 'it' the matter and 'over' finished.

clue.text: Nearly stop doctor taking ring in the capital

indicators.note: nearly means almost all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a colon is a punctuation stop
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A doctor almost halts a procedure while taking a ring off a patient in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' cuts the last letter from COLON, leaving COLO.
explanation.definitionFit: Colombo is the commercial capital and largest city of Sri Lanka.

clue.text: By which zealous patriot might express surprise or annoyance

definitions.text: By which zealous patriot might express surprise or annoyance

parts.words: By which zealous patriot might express surprise or annoyance
parts.note: the word wanted is both a name for a flag-waving patriot and the word completing an old-fashioned exclamation that begins with by

explanation.surface: A fervent nationalist is given to exclaiming in surprise or irritation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By jingo!' is a dated British exclamation of surprise; a jingoist is an aggressive patriot.
explanation.definitionFit: Jingo is a chauvinistic patriot, from a music-hall song, and the oath 'by jingo' expresses astonishment.

clue.text: Make-up used before battle

parts.note: cosmetics in the surface, but literally the colours warriors daubed on themselves ahead of fighting

explanation.surface: Someone applies heavy cosmetics before facing a tough confrontation.
explanation.definitionFit: Warriors traditionally painted faces and bodies before combat; humorously, heavy cosmetics.

clue.text: Why stray into boat? …

indicators.note: into means the second word goes inside the first word

parts.note: to err is to stray from the right path

explanation.surface: A puzzled observer asks why a vessel has drifted off course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Why' reads as the start of a question but is the clue's own word, used as letters; the ellipsis links to the next clue's boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A wherry is a light rowing boat or a broad sailing barge, such as those on the Norfolk Broads.

clue.text: … Flying boat?

parts.note: not a seaplane but any large passenger aircraft, a ship of the skies

explanation.surface: Someone asks about a seaplane, following on from the previous boat.
explanation.walkthrough: A flying boat is a real seaplane, but here the phrase is read loosely as a ship that flies.
explanation.definitionFit: A large passenger aircraft is a vessel that carries people through the air.

clue.text: Use this north of the border to go on board

definitions.text: Use this north of the border to go on board

parts.words: north of the border to go
parts.note: gang is the Scots verb for go, Scotland being north of the English border
a plank is a board

explanation.surface: Instructions for boarding a ship in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the ramp used to board, and also builds it from Scots GANG (go) and PLANK (board).
explanation.definitionFit: A gangplank is the movable walkway used for getting on and off a ship.

clue.text: A bit mad being in a separate room

parts.note: a part is a bit of something
mental is informal for mad

explanation.surface: Someone a little crazy is shut away in a room of their own.
explanation.definitionFit: Apartmental is a rare adjective relating to an apartment, a set of rooms apart from others.

clue.text: Make a beastly noise before taking the continental money

parts.note: a cow, a beast, lows or moos
la is French for the, a continental language

explanation.surface: A cow lows before a foreign coin is pocketed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The continental' asks for 'the' in a European language: French LA.
explanation.definitionFit: Moola is slang for cash, much like dough or bread.

clue.text: Relative one is not very close to

definitions.text: Relative one is not very close to

parts.words: Relative one is not very close to
parts.note: suggests a family member one has drifted apart from, but means a kin member remotely connected by descent

explanation.surface: Someone describes a family member they rarely speak to.
explanation.definitionFit: A remote kinsman, related only through several generations, is literally far off on the family tree.

clue.text: Citizen Edward was made liable

parts.note: a subject is a citizen of a monarchy
Ed is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A man named Edward has been held legally responsible.
explanation.definitionFit: To be subjected to something is to be exposed or made answerable to it.

clue.text: Standard document, type found in Malay boat

indicators.note: found in means the type word sits inside the boat word

parts.note: a proa is a fast Malay sailing boat
a form is a type or kind

explanation.surface: A standard form of paperwork is discovered aboard a Malaysian vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The proa is an outrigger sailing craft of the Malay archipelago, a word met mostly in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A pro forma is a standard template document, such as a preliminary invoice.

clue.text: This task is done over and over again

definitions.text: This task is done over and over again

parts.words: This task is done over and over again
parts.note: describes monotonous work, the same chore performed endlessly

explanation.surface: A worker complains of a monotonous chore.
explanation.definitionFit: Routine, monotonous work consisting of the same actions endlessly duplicated.

clue.text: Go off at this line?

parts.note: from the idiom about digressing suddenly, the geometric line touching a curve at one point

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to depart at this railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'go off at a tangent' means to digress; the line is the geometric one.
explanation.definitionFit: A straight line touching a curve at a single point, from the idiom for abrupt digression.

clue.text: Lady embraced a new queen in Europe

indicators.note: embraced means the lady's name wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: Julia is a lady's name

explanation.surface: A woman hugs a newly crowned European queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Juliana was Queen of the Netherlands from 1948 to 1980.

clue.text: Supporter in the long run?

explanation.surface: A backer who stays loyal over the years.
explanation.walkthrough: A stayer is a horse or runner with stamina for long races; the question mark marks the playful second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay is a prop, so one that holds up is a backer; a racehorse with stamina excels over long distances.

clue.text: Give enough time to belong

explanation.surface: Make time for a newcomer so they feel at home.
explanation.definitionFit: To squeeze an appointment into a schedule; to be accepted naturally as part of a group.

clue.text: Musicians do not make any noise when obeying this instruction

definitions.text: Musicians do not make any noise when obeying this instruction

parts.words: Musicians do not make any noise when obeying this instruction
parts.note: a direction in a score telling a player or section to stay silent

explanation.surface: An orchestra falls silent at a conductor's direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacet, Latin for 'is silent', is the score marking telling a performer to rest.

clue.text: Record symbolised said signing up formally

parts.note: to enrol is to enter on a record or register

indicators.note: said means the following word is spoken, giving letters that match its sound

parts.note: a thing symbolised is what was meant

explanation.surface: A record is kept of what a formal signing stood for.
explanation.definitionFit: Enrolment is official registration, as on a course or in an army.

clue.text: Reproduce acer tree anew

indicators.note: anew means the letters of acer and tree are made again in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A gardener propagates a maple tree once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To create again is to reproduce or remake something.

clue.text: Outdated lines in confectionery

parts.note: something past its time is outdated
RY, railway, is a crossword abbreviation for lines

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned rows of sweets are displayed in a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastry, as in cakes and tarts, is sweet baked confectionery.

clue.text: Stay with lute playing in a shrewd manner

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of stay and lute are messed about with

explanation.surface: A musician persists with the lute, playing it cleverly.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewdly and cannily, showing sharp judgement.

clue.text: Invader finds assistant in luxury car

indicators.note: in means the assistant is placed inside the car

parts.note: RR is Rolls-Royce, the luxury car
an aide is an assistant

explanation.surface: An intruder discovers a helper sitting in a Rolls-Royce.
explanation.walkthrough: Rolls-Royce is abbreviated by its two initials, a common crossword shorthand for a luxury car.
explanation.definitionFit: A raider attacks and invades enemy territory.
